title: Quick Dense Japanese Scallion Gyoza
description: A fresh and dense Japanese dish featuring scallions, this recipe is a nostalgic take on traditional gyoza, made keto-friendly with careful ingredient selection.

ingredients.name: wonton wrappers
ingredients.notes: low-carb, made from almond flour or similar

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, chopped scallions, grated ginger, and minced garlic, mixing well with your hands or a wooden spoon until just combined.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, and xanthan gum to the pork mixture, mixing until the ingredients are evenly distributed.
Lay a wonton wrapper on a clean surface, placing a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.

Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wonton wrapper, then fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point, pressing the edges together to seal the gyoza.
Repeat the process with the remaining wonton wrappers and filling, making sure to seal the gyoza tightly to prevent leakage during cooking.
Heat the coconut oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, then add the gyoza to the skillet, being careful not to overcrowd it.
Cook the gyoza for 2-3 minutes on each side, until they are golden brown and crispy, adjusting the heat as necessary to prevent burning.
Serve the gyoza hot with your favorite dipping sauce, garnished with additional chopped scallions if desired.
